findings.claim: A formatted type's own MessagePack attributes are ignored unless the caller duplicates its contract in a surrogate. In the no-surrogate path, the collector unconditionally builds members with CreateContractlessMembers. For example, a type with [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)], [Key(0)] on Value, and [IgnoreMember] on Ignored gets a contractless string-key formatter that serializes Ignored, instead of the required [Key]/[IgnoreMember] behaviour.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.Req2129ReceiptTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursMessagePackAttributes. It generates a formatter for an attributed type and fails on head because generated source still contains the [IgnoreMember] property. A runtime companion can serialize the same object and show that Ignored is written and that string keys are used instead of the declared integer key.

findings.claim: The timestamp32 eligibility mask was inverted. nanoseconds shifted left by 34 always leaves the low 32 bits clear, so every positive-subsecond timestamp whose Unix seconds value is zero now takes the timestamp32 branch and loses its subsecond component. For example, 1970-01-01T00:00:00.500Z round-trips as 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z; a seconds value of 2^32 is likewise truncated by the 32-bit encoding.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.Req2129ReceiptTests.TimestampAtEpochWithSubsecondsRoundTrips. It serializes and deserializes 1970-01-01T00:00:00.500Z using MessagePackSerializer and fails on head because the result is the epoch without the 500 milliseconds. Also assert that an integral timestamp at Unix second 0 uses timestamp32 while a subsecond timestamp at that second uses timestamp64.
